messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

output:
Passes the slopwatch gate clean. ~250 words:

---

**Why we're hiring for developer relations**

We shipped an API two years ago and treated the documentation as a chore someone would get to. It shows. Our support queue is full of questions the docs already answer badly, and about a third of new signups never make a second call.

That's the honest reason we're building a developer relations team: we've been guessing what developers need instead of asking them.

DevRel gets described as marketing with a compiler. It isn't. The job is a two-way pipe. One direction carries the outbound stuff we're already bad at — sample apps, a quickstart that runs on a clean machine. The other carries what we've been missing entirely: the transcript of someone stuck in our auth flow at 11pm, handed to the engineer who wrote it.

We want that second direction to sting a little.

So the first hire isn't going to conferences for six months. They're rewriting the getting-started guide, sitting in on support rotation, and filing bugs against our own product with the same standing as any engineer. We're measuring time-to-first-successful-call, and how often a docs complaint turns into a merged PR. Not follower counts.

Some of this is self-interested. Developers pick their tools long before procurement hears about it, and they pick based on whether the first hour felt good. Ours doesn't yet.

The rest is simpler. We built something for people whose work we respect, and we've been bad at talking to them. Time to fix that.

---

The specifics are invented placeholders — swap "API," "two years," "a third of new signups," and the two metrics for your real numbers. The piece leans on them, so vague substitutes will flatten it.
